extracted.intended_audience: physicians and other clinicians caring for patients with motor neurone disease (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, progressive bulbar palsy)
extracted.subtask_description: Clinical management recommendations for relieving symptoms and improving quality of life in patients with motor neurone disease, including terminal-stage care and choices between home and hospice care. Emphasis is on symptomatic treatment, physician responsibilities, and palliative principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symptomatic treatments to relieve symptoms and disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in the most severe forms of motor neurone disease...the symptoms and disabilities from progressive paralysis may be relieved in many patients by various symptomatic treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a range of symptomatic interventions to address specific disabilities from progressive paralysis; individualize treatment choices to patient needs and potential benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve quality of life even in the terminal stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of life may be improved even in the terminal stage...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue active symptom management and supportive measures during terminal stages with the goal of maximizing comfort and quality of life rather than withdrawing care solely because of disease stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of narcotic administration in terminal stage
rubrics_metrics.description: When narcotic administration should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use opioid analgesia as appropriate for relief of severe symptoms (e.g., pain, dyspnea) in terminal patients, balancing symptom control and monitoring for side effects; discuss risks/benefits with patient/family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician's role: offer and carefully supervise treatments, not withhold them
rubrics_metrics.description: The physician's proper role is to offer and carefully supervise these treatments, not withhold them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively propose symptomatic and palliative options, provide close follow-up and supervision, and avoid withholding interventions that can relieve symptoms; involve patient/family in shared decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home care recommended even for the most severely paralysed
rubrics_metrics.description: Home care is recommended even for the most severely paralysed, though hospice care may be a good alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize home-based care when feasible, arranging resources/supports to maintain patients at home; consider hospice care as an appropriate alternative depending on patient needs, preferences, and available services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching principle: alleviate symptoms for all progressive incurable diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying principle--to alleviate symptoms--applies to the management of all progressive incurable diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt symptom relief and comfort as the guiding aim of care planning across incurable progressive conditions, guiding treatment selection and goals of care discussions.
